epithet: A letter to Makkah, and where loyalty lies
lede: On the eve of the conquest a veteran of Badr sent a secret warning to Quraysh, to protect his family there. The letter was intercepted. What came down about it is one of the Qurʾan’s most careful lessons: firm on the principle, gentle with the man — and exact about who is, and is not, an enemy.

names.name: al-Mumtaḥanah
names.note: After its tenth ayah, which commands that believing women who emigrate be examined. Al-Qurṭubī notes that it is also read al-Mumtaḥinah, “the examiner” — the surah itself, which tests. It is sometimes called Sūrat al-Imtiḥān.

revelation.detail: It is Madinan in the saying of all. Its opening came down about Ḥāṭib ibn Abī Baltaʿah, as the Prophet ﷺ was preparing to march on Makkah in the eighth year; its tenth ayah belongs to the time of the truce of al-Ḥudaybiyah, two years earlier, when believing women began to arrive from Makkah. The traditional order places it ninety-first.
revelation.when: Madinah, between the truce of al-Ḥudaybiyah and the conquest of Makkah — the sixth to the eighth year

evidence.quote: كَانَ سَبَبُ نُزُولِ صَدْرِ هَذِهِ السُّورَةِ الْكَرِيمَةِ قِصَّةَ حَاطِبِ بْنِ أَبِي بَلْتَعَةَ، وَذَلِكَ أَنَّ حَاطِبًا هَذَا كَانَ رَجُلًا مِنَ الْمُهَاجِرِينَ، وَكَانَ مِنْ أَهْلِ بَدْرٍ أَيْضًا

attested.quote: أخْرَجَ ابْنُ الضُّرَيْسِ، والنَّحّاسُ، وابْنُ مَرْدُويَهْ، والبَيْهَقِيُّ، عَنِ ابْنِ عَبّاسٍ قالَ: نَزَلَتْ سُورَةُ «المُمْتَحَنَةِ» بِالمَدِينَةِ
attested.says: Ibn ʿAbbās: it came down in Madinah. Recorded by Ibn al-Ḍurays, al-Naḥḥās, Ibn Mardawayh and al-Bayhaqī.

setting: Quraysh had broken the truce, and the Prophet ﷺ was quietly readying an army to take Makkah before they could prepare — hoping, by surprise, to take it without a slaughter. Ḥāṭib ibn Abī Baltaʿah knew of it. He was an Emigrant who had fought at Badr; but unlike the other Emigrants he was not of Quraysh by blood, and his family in Makkah had no clan to protect them. He wrote to the leaders of Quraysh telling them what was coming, and gave the letter to a woman travelling south.

ʿAlī tells the rest. “The Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent me, al-Zubayr and al-Miqdād, saying: ride until you reach the meadow of Khākh; there you will find a woman in a litter with a letter. Take it from her.” They found her; she denied having anything; they told her to produce it or be searched, and she drew it from her braids.

The Prophet ﷺ asked: “Ḥāṭib, what is this?” He said: do not be hasty with me, Messenger of Allah. I was a man attached to Quraysh, not one of them. The Emigrants with you have kin there to protect their families; I had none, and wanted to do them a favour by which they would protect mine. I did not do it out of disbelief, nor to leave my religion. The Prophet ﷺ said: “He has told you the truth.” ʿUmar asked leave to strike his neck. He said: “He was present at Badr. How do you know? Perhaps Allah has looked upon the people of Badr and said: do as you will, for I have forgiven you.”
Then the surah came down — addressing Ḥāṭib, even in his fault, with “O you who believe”.

occasions.title: Ḥāṭib’s letter
occasions.text: ʿAlī said: the Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent me, al-Zubayr and al-Miqdād, and said: “Ride until you come to the meadow of Khākh. There is a woman there, travelling by camel, who has a letter with her; take it from her.” We set off, our horses racing under us, until we reached the meadow, and there was the woman. We said: “Bring out the letter.” She said: “I have no letter.” We said: “You will bring out the letter, or we shall strip you of your clothes.” And she drew it out from the plaits of her hair.
story: We brought it to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. It was from Ḥāṭib ibn Abī Baltaʿah to some of the idolaters in Makkah, telling them something of what the Messenger of Allah ﷺ intended. He said: “Ḥāṭib, what is this?” He said: “Messenger of Allah, do not be hasty with me. I was a man attached to Quraysh — an ally of theirs, and not one of them by blood. The Emigrants who are with you have kinsmen there who protect their families and their property. Since I lacked that tie of blood among them, I wished to do them a service for which they would protect my kin. I did not do it to turn back from my religion, nor because I am content with disbelief after Islam.” The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “He has told you the truth.”

ʿUmar said: “Messenger of Allah, let me strike the neck of this hypocrite.” He ﷺ said: “He was at Badr. And what do you know? Perhaps Allah looked upon those who were at Badr and said: Do what you will, for I have forgiven you.” And Allah sent down the surah: “O you who believe, do not take My enemy and your enemy as allies, offering them affection…” as far as “he has strayed from the right way.”
occasions.source: ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib: al-Bukhārī (4274, 4890) and Muslim (2494).

occasions.title: Asmāʾ and her mother
occasions.text: Asmāʾ bint Abī Bakr said: “My mother came to me, while she was still an idolater, in the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. I asked him: my mother has come to me hoping for my kindness — shall I keep ties with her?” He said: “Yes. Keep ties with your mother.”
occasions.source: Asmāʾ bint Abī Bakr: al-Bukhārī (2620) and Muslim (1003).

occasions.title: The women who emigrated
occasions.text: After the truce, believing women came to Madinah as emigrants, and their families demanded them back under its terms. They were examined as to their faith and not returned. ʿĀʾishah said: the Messenger of Allah ﷺ would examine them by this ayah; whoever accepted its conditions, he would say to her, “I have accepted your pledge” — in words only. By Allah, his hand never touched the hand of a woman in taking the pledge.

aim: To free the hearts of the believers from loyalty to anything other than the religion of Allah.
themes: Kindness to those who do not fight you

outline.title: Do not take My enemy as an ally
outline.summary: O you who believe, do not take My enemy and your enemy as allies, offering them affection when they have rejected the truth that has come to you, and driven out the Messenger and yourselves because you believe in Allah. If they got the better of you they would be your enemies. Neither your kin nor your children will benefit you on the Day of Resurrection.

outline.title: The example of Ibrāhīm
outline.summary: There is an excellent example for you in Ibrāhīm and those with him, when they said to their people: “We are free of you and of what you worship besides Allah.” And their prayer: “Our Lord, upon You we rely, to You we turn, and to You is the journey’s end. Our Lord, do not make us a trial for those who disbelieve.”

outline.title: Who is, and is not, an enemy
outline.summary: It may be that Allah will put affection between you and those you now hold as enemies. Allah does not forbid you, concerning those who have not fought you over religion nor driven you from your homes, to deal kindly and justly with them: Allah loves the just (60:8). He forbids you only to take as allies those who fought you over religion, drove you out, or helped in driving you out.

outline.title: The believing women who emigrate
outline.summary: When believing women come to you as emigrants, examine them — Allah knows best their faith. If you find them to be believers, do not send them back to the disbelievers: they are not lawful for them, nor are those lawful for these. Give the husbands what they spent. And do not hold to marriage ties with disbelieving women.

outline.title: The women’s pledge
outline.summary: O Prophet, when believing women come to pledge to you that they will associate nothing with Allah, will not steal, will not commit unlawful intercourse, will not kill their children, will not bring a slander they have invented, and will not disobey you in what is right — accept their pledge, and ask Allah to forgive them. And, once more: do not ally yourselves with a people with whom Allah is angry.

keyAyah.why: The balance to everything before it. Disavowing an enemy’s religion is not a licence to be unjust or unkind to those who have done you no harm.

before: Al-Ḥashr showed hypocrites allied with an enemy inside Madinah. Al-Mumtaḥanah addresses a sincere believer who, for his family’s sake, reached out to the enemy outside it.
after: This surah set the believers’ loyalty in order. Al-Ṣaff asks them to act on it: Allah loves those who fight in His cause in ranks, like a wall firmly joined.
